PistonPeak.badMapRefComparison: Inspected against bad-map-refs/1, 9, 10 and 11. Not a flat sprinkled field: the route is two 8.8-17.4 stud columns stacked five deep, not a wide open deck. No repeated narrow swing-panel bypass and no lone open spinner: each of the seven beats carries a different mechanic and the coverage audit found no hazard-free 24x24 square. No empty slabs: the only unhazarded runs are the box_011 climbs, which are the course's own elevation change. No avoidable or floating bumpers: all nine bumper slabs stagger across their own deck and are scored as three chicane encounters.
PistonPeak.method: CourseAuthoring.preview put an unregistered clone at the live MapOrigin; the clone alone was lifted 9,000 studs, the camera was posed through workspace.CurrentCamera at FieldOfView 70, and the viewport was grabbed to a real PNG. clearPreview() removed the clone afterwards; workspace.Assets.Arena.Map.Model was never moved and is still at its recorded pivot.

SummitSplash.badMapRefComparison: Inspected against bad-map-refs/1, 2, 9, 10 and 11. Reference 2 IS the pre-hardening Summit and is 8.6's readability bar for this course, so the comparison is a before/after rather than an avoid-this. NOT a flat sprinkled field (ref 1): the route is an eight-storey climbing arc, and the hazards are grouped into 13 walled gates instead of the even scatter ref 2 shows. No repeated narrow swing-panel bypass: there is no swing panel, and every gate is a different recipe. No lone open spinner (ref 10): every windmill and mace now stands inside a measured wall pair that closes both edge strips at its own angle. No avoidable or floating bumpers (ref 11): all five bumpers sit on the deck at a measured +0.00 and every one of them spans the route centreline at rest. WHERE IT IS STILL CLOSEST TO THE BAD REFERENCES, stated plainly: the preserved 44-stud arc deck between gates is open coloured slab with nothing on it, which is ref 10 and 11's empty-slab look. That is the same preserved geometry the NoBreatherSquare finding measures and the same geometry 7.7 forbids redesigning. Readability itself is better than ref 2: the green gate walls punctuate the lane into readable doorways, and the narrowed inward bridge reads as a real crossing instead of the 46-stud free walk in ref 2's foreground.

note: Fixed-camera captures for HANDOFF 8.6, one entry per course. The prescribed offsets are relative to the course's own origin: top-down eye (0,520,1) looking at (0,20,0); three-quarter eye (300,260,300) looking at (0,20,0), both at 70 degrees. The preview is lifted 9,000 studs above MapOrigin for the shots, because the arena's own hazard ring and PvP floor sit at MapOrigin and fill the frame; the camera offsets are unchanged, so the framing is the prescribed one with an empty background.
